nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni1-xFex(OH)y LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: nickel(II) nitrate hexahydrate Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and iron(II) sulfate heptahydrate FeSO4·7H2O in a specific molar ratio (Ni2++Fe2+=1 mmol) were dissolved in 35 mL deionized water, followed by the addition of 300 mg urea and 120 mg ammonium fluoride. After stirring for 30 min, the suspension was transferred to a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated at 120 °C for 10 h before cooling to room temperature. The resultant precipitate was centrifuged and washed with deionized water and ethanol and dried at 60 °C for 1 h. The doping level of Fe atoms was controlled by precisely regulating the molar ratio of Ni/Fe salts.

nodes.name: Thermal sulfidation of LDH to pyrite Ni1-xFexS2
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared Ni1-xFex(OH)y LDH was sufficiently mixed with sulphur powder (Alfa Aesar, ~100 mesh, 99.5%, 1:5 weight ratio) by grinding for 30 min. The mixture was then placed in the center of a quartz tube in an aluminum oxide boat, and heated at 400 °C for 1 h in an argon atmosphere to obtain pyrite-type Ni1-xFexS2. Finally, the obtained compounds were ultrasonicated, washed several times and dried under vacuum overnight.

nodes.source_text: The steady-state linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) in N₂-saturated 1 M KOH, as shown in Fig. 3c, demonstrates that NiS₂ exhibits an overpotential of 241 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻². As the Fe doping amount x increases before reaching 0.2, the corresponding overpotential @10 mA cm⁻² continues to decrease to 121 mV... The Tafel slope... compared with 123 mV dec⁻¹ for NiS₂, Ni₀.₈Fe₀.₂S₂ (x = 0.2) shows... Tafel slope as low as 55 mV dec⁻¹... Nyquist plots... R_ct of NiS₂ [45.6 Ω], and Ni₀.₈Fe₀.₂S₂ shows... 9.8 Ω... double-layer capacitance C_dl of Ni₀.₈Fe₀.₂S₂ (53.28 mF cm⁻²) compared with NiS₂ (22.7 mF cm⁻²)... TOF of Ni₀.₈Fe₀.₂S₂ is ∼19.4 fold higher than NiS₂ at... 200 mV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD patterns of the synthesized Ni₁₋ₓFeₓS₂ (x ≈ 0-0.33) samples match standard cubic (Pa-3) pyrite-type materials (JCPDS No. 65-3325). Diffraction peak shifts to larger angle with increasing Fe substitution due to lattice parameter changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 2a, the diffraction peaks of the as-prepared Ni₁₋ₓFeₓS₂ match with those of standard cubic (Pa-3) pyrite-type materials (JCPDS No. 65-3325). Furthermore, the diffraction peak exhibits a shift to a large angle with increasing Fe substitution.

nodes.characterization_summary: k³-weighted Fourier transform Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra show peaks I and II at ~1.9 Å (Ni-S) and ~3.5 Å (Ni-Ni). Fe substitution weakens first-shell Ni-S peak, indicating lower nickel-sulfide coordination number and more sulphur vacancies.

FT Ni K-edge EXAFS analysis in Fig. 2f (right axis), two separate peaks (peaks I and II) at ~1.9 and 3.5 Å are assigned to the features of Ni–S and Ni–Ni bonds ... the first-shell peak I is weakened by Fe substitution, suggesting a lower nickel-sulfide coordination number (CN), more sulphur vacancies.
